handfixes.summary: The bulk writes (rerun-failed --yes, import) pass a seeded crash-and-retry simulation: 200 seeds against a fake Comet Server that answers, refuses (5xx, 4xx), drops the connection, answers late, answers an empty 200 or a 200 failure envelope, with two parallel runs, a run cancelled mid-flight, a rerun and a healthy rerun. Four fixes it forced: rerun-failed plans and dispatches under one dispatch lock per OS account; the server version fails closed; import counts a record only on a 2xx Comet Status and --idempotent skips records that exist; storage is not importable; every Comet client drops Idempotency-Key headers so no write is replayed.
handfixes.why: Repo rule: a command that writes into live customer data in bulk ships only after a crash-and-retry simulation proves it never acts twice and never exits 0 while work is missing. On the original code the simulation found: two parallel rerun-failed --yes runs dispatched the same backups twice (R1); a {"Status":403} envelope on meta/version read as an old server and dispatched scheduled rules for custom-run failures (R1); import counted an empty 200 or a message-less failure envelope as created and exited 0 with the record missing (I2); import ignored --idempotent, so a rerun after a crash could never finish (I3); import storage created the same Storage Vault again on every rerun (I1), and no request field lets Comet refuse a duplicate, so it was removed. The --idempotent pre-read must fail through fleetError: classifyAPIError's 409 no-op made a refused read exit 0 with nothing imported. The client replays a POST after an ambiguous failure only when an Idempotency-Key or X-Idempotency-Key header is present (client.go canRetryAmbiguousFailure, even with X-Printing-Press-Replay-Safe false); Comet ignores the header, so a config [headers] entry would have re-sent a dispatch up to three times. Each fix was reverted and its test watched fail. COMET_WRITE_SIM_SEEDS=1500 runs a longer soak. Publish Codex r1 + adversarial r1: the dispatch lock was keyed by the server URL as typed and lived in the per-home state dir, so host vs host:443, 127.0.0.1 vs localhost, or two COMET_BACKUP_HOME values dispatched the same backup twice; the lock is now one per user under the home directory. The per-home lock location is superseded by rerun-dispatch-lock (one lock per OS account).

handfixes.summary: The shared credential kit (tools/maintainer/credkit, vendored at cli/internal/credkit) is wired by hand and replaces this connector's own funnel, chokepoint and SQLite wrapper. internal/credwire/declarations.go holds the one Declarations literal; each main starts with credkit.Start and ends with credkit.Exit; the API client goes through credkit.Transport under the origin pin and inside the response redactor, so the kit reads the server's own bytes and never reads the [redacted] marker as a credential; every file write except the 0600 credential store and config file goes through the kit (cliutil.AtomicWriteCredentialFile is that declared exemption); stdout and stderr are the kit's pipes. The MCP server's CLI children run through credkit.RunCommand, which hands each child the held set. Documents the kit's sources do not reach (a request body before a preview, MCP arguments, an import record, a --stdin body) go to credkit.HoldBody through cliutil.HoldDocument; no reader of the connector's own.
handfixes.why: One contract, one matcher and one set of sinks replace the connector-only copies, and a matcher fix reaches this connector by vendoring. A Comet Server's host is the MSP's, so no hosted domain can be named: credentialFiles shows the kit this process's server (COMET_BACKUP_BASE_URL, COMET_BACKUP_SERVER, config) through COMET_BACKUP_BASE_URL for the duration of Start, and AfterStart puts the variable back. When nothing resolves the kit allows no origin. Tests: internal/cometblackbox (built binaries against a stub that echoes every credential in every encoding), internal/credwire.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: generate the Start and Exit prologue, the Declarations literal from the spec's auth and credential fields, and the credential hand-off for CLI children.

handfixes.summary: Credential-named members of a Comet response are held, then replaced by [redacted] before any command reads the body, so a credential-tier read still prints its records. Every member of a duplicate key and every component of a credential value (form and query values, cookie values, a URL's password, an auth header's token at any length) is held.
handfixes.why: The kit withholds a whole unit that carries a held value. Without the redactor every record-bearing read of a Comet profile or organization would print only the kit's notice.

handfixes.summary: A --stdin body is held from its raw bytes before the command parses it, previews and --dry-run included, then re-piped to the command.

handfixes.why: The map keeps only the last of a duplicate member and a broken line never reaches the request hold, so a server refusal or parse error could repeat the lost value.

handfixes.summary: The date-range read ends a day past this machine's clock.
handfixes.why: Comet filters on its own clock (comet-go-sdk: only jobs started or ended in range). With that clock ahead, a just-started backup was missing and rerun-failed planned its failed predecessor again.

handfixes.summary: rerun-failed records a dispatch before sending it and clears it on an answer. One left behind (a killed run, a lost reply, a 5xx) is reported unconfirmed and not sent again for 30 minutes. A future-dated intent (the clock moved back) keeps refusing.
handfixes.why: The lock is released when a run dies, and a job may not show yet, so a waiting run planned and sent the same backup again.

handfixes.summary: A password inside base_url is held whatever raw characters it carries, from the environment, the server variable or config.
handfixes.why: A raw / # or ? ends the authority for a URL parser and the kit's own reader, so the password went unheld and the connection error printed it.

handfixes.summary: A mirrored write's preview drops a caller's dry-run argument, so its own --dry-run is the one the child reads.
handfixes.why: The last flag wins, and dry-run false after the preview's --dry-run sent the write with no confirm.

handfixes.summary: a row the credential kit withholds from the store is skipped and named; the rest of the batch is stored and sync keeps walking, then ends that resource failed with the row ids
handfixes.why: One withheld row aborted the whole batch transaction, and sync returned on it, so a single large ordinary record (or one that really carried a held credential) stopped the resource and every row after it was never synced (#612, hubspot-calls-crm). The row is still withheld; it is now named in a sync_error event and in the resource's error, the run exits non-zero, and the watermark stays so the next run fetches it again. Re-applied after a reprint by replay_handfixes.py (recipe withheld-rows).
